messages:
alice: Heads up — noticed LCP and chart paint times jump on /dashboard canary after last deploy. Heatmap and sparklines freeze ~1.6-2s on first interaction. :eyes:
ben: Which deploy? canary id? Was it a client change or infra routing tweak?
alice: Canary 2026-03-19-telemetry-rollout. Two changes landed: telemetry sampler + a prefetch routing tweak that forces chart workers to inline more chunks.
carla: Measured bundle delta — main bundle + telemetry import = +185KB, plus worker chunk duplication on some routes (~120KB extra). local trace attached (short snippet):
```
Network: GET /static/js/main.abc.js 200 1420ms
Network: GET /static/js/worker.chunk.js 200 620ms
Network: GET /static/js/telemetry.client.js 200 150ms
// same worker chunk pulled twice due to different chunk names across routes
```
deepa: We also changed prefetch policy to eager for the heatmap route last night (prefetch: true -> eager). That increases concurrency and seems to surface duplicate vendor chunks when chunk names collide.
frank: sre-bot shows CDN cache key changed for chunking on 2026-03-19 02:14 UTC, probably due to the build config change (chunkFilename pattern switched). :boom:
sre-bot: deploy-2026-03-19: build-config bump -> chunkFilename set to [name].[hash].js across repos. Observed inconsistent content hash for identical modules because of dynamic imports order variance.
ben: So tolerable explanation: telemetry import increased main payload + prefetch change caused duplication + chunk naming produced mismatched caches -> double-downloads -> paint stall.
carla: Quick repro steps I used: load /dashboard in incognito, throttle 3G, record network waterfall. See double GETs for worker chunk when navigating from /teams -> /dashboard.
alice: Can we hotfix this in canary? Options: revert telemetry sampler import (lazy-load it) OR revert prefetch policy OR make chunk names deterministic.
frank: Fastest partial fix: lazy-load telemetry and gate with feature flag. That removes +185KB sync cost. I can open a patch for telemetry -> dynamic import.
carla: Patch idea (example):
```
// old
import telemetry from 'telemetry/client';
// new
const telemetry = () => import(/* webpackChunkName: "telemetry-client" */ 'telemetry/client');
// then await telemetry() when actually sending events
```
deepa: If we lazy-load telemetry we still have the duplicate worker chunk problem from prefetch churn. I'd prefer toggling prefetch for the heatmap route back to 'link' for canary 0–10%.
ben: Agreed. Rollout plan: 1) quick telemetry lazy-load patch to canary immediately; 2) revert prefetch to link for canary 100% rollback if telemetry patch insufficient; 3) longer term: fix chunkNaming to [contenthash:8] and enable deterministic chunking plugin.
alice: Can we run a small A/B: telemetry lazy + prefetch revert on 10% traffic and compare LCP telemetry?
frank: I can push lazy patch in 10m. frank: /deploy canary telemetry-lazy-4367001234 --tag=telemetry-lazy
sre-bot: deploy started by frank: canary telemetry-lazy-4367001234. Logs: build ok, route update -> CDN purge scheduled.
carla: Meanwhile I'll open a PR to enforce deterministic chunk names and add a test to catch cross-route duplication. PR: github.com/redwood/console/pull/5804 (WIP).
deepa: Also let's add a quick client-side guard to skip duplicate downloads: check a global registry for loaded chunk ids before fetching worker. Might be hacky but low-risk short term.
ben: Good. After canary runs for 30m with 10% traffic and we see LCP back to baseline, we can promote. If not, revert the canary totally.
alice: Thanks — appreciate the fast triage. I'll monitor real-user LCP in console and post numbers. :thumbsup:
frank: FYI for docs/infra: avoid switching chunkFilename patterns across minor builds; it causes cache fragmentation. I'll add a note to the build pipeline.
carla: Also adding a telemetry test to our perf harness to surface import-size regressions in PRs (threshold 100KB).
alice: Update: after telemetry lazy patch landed on canary for 10% traffic, initial LCP samples show 430ms -> down from 1.8s. More numbers in 15m.
frank: :party: good start.
(emoji reactions scattered: :eyes:, :thumbsup:, :rocket:)
